rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nitrogen's oxyacids are a staircase of oxidation states: **H₂N₂O₂** (hyponitrous, N +1), **HNO₂** (nitrous, N +3 — a solution-only, unstable acid with dual redox behaviour, whose nitrite salts cure meats and diazotise dyes), **HNO₃** (nitric, N +5 — the strong, fully-ionised, resonance-stabilised flagship), and the unstable peroxo **HNO₄** (pernitric).…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Nitrogen Wears More Hats Than Any Element Nitrogen's oxidation states run +1 to +5, and each has its oxyacid: HNO₂ (nitrous), HNO₃ (nitric), plus hyponitrous H₂N₂O₂, nitroxylic H₂N₂O₄ and pernitric HNO₄. This topic names and formulas them, then zooms into nitric acid — the Ostwald process (verified NEB 2021) and its oxidising chemistry.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The oxyacids of nitrogen — name and formula table | Oxidation state | Formula | Name | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | +1 | H₂N₂O₂ | Hyponitrous acid | Weak, unstable; salts = hyponitrites | | +2 | HNO₂ | Nitrous acid | Known only in solution; salts = nitrites (NaNO₂, KNO₂) | | +3 | HNO₂ | (same as +2: N is +3 in HNO₂) — see below | — | | +3 | HNO₃? No — HNO₃ is +5 | — | — | | +4 |…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Oxidation-state sums: HNO2 = +3, HNO3 = +5, H2N2O2 = +1 each. Ostwald trio: NH3->NO (Pt-Rh 800-900 C), NO->NO2, NO2->HNO3 (NO recycled). Conc = NO2, dil = NO, very dil + Zn = NH4NO3. Aqua regia 3:1 dissolves gold. Passive: Fe, Al, Cr in conc.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Concentration decides the reduction depth: the same nitric acid hands metals NO₂ when concentrated, NO when dilute, and N₂O or NH₄⁺ when very dilute with active metals — quote the condition with every equation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Oxyacid ladder: H2N2O2 hyponitrous (N +1), HNO2 nitrous (N +3, solution-only, unstable, dual redox), HNO3 nitric (N +5, strong, oxidant), HNO4 pernitric (N +5 peroxo, unstable). Ostwald: 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O (Pt-Rh gauze 800-900 C, ~10% NH3 in air below explosive limit); 2NO + O2 -> 2NO2; 3NO2 + H2O -> 2HNO3 + NO…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Global nitric acid output exceeds 50 million tonnes a year — nearly all of it feeding fertiliser and explosive manufacture through ammonium nitrate.

rows.text: Explain why Al containers can store concentrated HNO3.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Oxidation state bookkeeping:** students mislabel HNO₂ as N(+2); arithmetic gives +3 (H +1, O −2). Write the sum before labelling.  ·  **HNO₂ is not a bottle acid:** it exists only in solution and decomposes on standing — "prepare in situ" is the correct phrasing.
